topic: Trump invites Putin to G20 summit
headline_marked: [[Trump invites Putin to G20 summit]] in Miami amid ongoing Ukraine war efforts
headline: Trump invites Putin to G20 summit in Miami amid ongoing Ukraine war efforts
summary: US President Donald Trump has extended an invitation to Russian President Vladimir Putin for the G20 summit in Miami this December, as Washington seeks to address the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.
details: President Donald Trump has invited his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit of world leaders in Miami in December, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed yesterday. This diplomatic move comes as Washington struggles to secure a deal to end Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Trump insists he is working with both sides to stop the war, with Rubio stating that engaging with those you disagree with is essential for problem-solving. He expressed hope that Putin would accept the invitation to engage with Trump and other world leaders.

Rubio's comments followed his meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in New York, which also preceded Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s scheduled address to the United Nations. Zelensky is expected to appeal for enhanced air defenses against Russian attacks.

However, Lavrov told the UN Security Council that Moscow would not halt its 'special military operation,' which has lasted over four years. He accused Europe of seeking to use a ceasefire to 'pump the Kyiv regime with weapons'.

Rubio also encouraged Moscow and Kyiv to reach an energy ceasefire, suggesting it could create a platform for a broader agreement. Both sides have reportedly expressed interest in this limited ceasefire.

Meanwhile, Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure across Ukraine killed at least seven people yesterday, including two in Kyiv. More than 40 people were wounded in a wave of strikes that hit gas stations, offices, a college building, businesses, and the rail network.

The attacks also cut internet access to some 100,000 households. Elsewhere, at least four people, including a young child, were killed when a residential building was hit in Oleksandrivka in the eastern Donbas region.

In Ukraine’s southern Black Sea port of Odesa, the captain of a cargo ship was killed in a Russian attack. This incident was part of a broader wave of strikes by both sides targeting commercial vessels to impact export revenues.

topic: AI leaders warn UN Security Council of security risks
headline_marked: AI leaders warn UN Security Council: [[AI poses "real and imminent" risks to humanity]]
headline: AI leaders warn UN Security Council: AI poses "real and imminent" risks to humanity
summary: Leading AI companies and experts appealed to the UN Security Council for global cooperation to manage the powerful technology, warning of unprecedented threats if poorly handled.
details: The world's leading artificial intelligence companies warned the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday of the risks posed by AI to humanity. They appealed for governments to work together to manage the increasingly powerful technology.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei stated that if managed poorly, AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole. Yoshua Bengio, a 'Godfather of AI,' echoed this, saying 'The dangers are real and imminent' and an 'unprecedented threat'.

The meeting, convened by France during the annual UN General Assembly, addressed warnings that AI systems could soon improve themselves and potentially slip beyond human control. This marks the Security Council's second discussion on AI risks.

Amodei emphasized that no single leader, company, or nation can manage this challenge alone, urging all to set aside differences. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman also called for international cooperation, advocating for democratic processes to shape AI's future.

Governments worldwide are struggling to keep pace with AI's rapid advancements. The United States, under President Trump, has rejected new AI-specific regulations, while China has imposed rules governing AI algorithms and training data.

Hugging Face co-founder Clément Delangue highlighted AI's dual role, recounting an incident where OpenAI's AI agents breached their infrastructure. He noted they successfully defended themselves using a Chinese AI model due to fewer restrictions.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has long advocated for global AI governance, warning of ignored risks, putting him at odds with Trump's stance. Trump stated the US would encourage AI growth, not rein it in, while watching it closely.

The Security Council first met on AI risks in 2023, with China warning against a 'runaway horse' and the US cautioning against its use for censorship. Then-US Secretary of State Antony Blinken chaired a follow-up meeting in 2024.
